title: Superpolynomial semidefinite extension complexity of perfect matching
formal: For every \(C,c>0\), does some even \(n\ge 2\) satisfy \(xc_{\mathrm{SDP}}(\mathrm{P}_{n})>Cn^{c}\), where \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) is the perfect-matching polytope of \(K_{n}\)?
definitions: \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\subseteq \mathbb{R}\)^(n choose 2) is the convex hull of the zero-one incidence vectors of all perfect matchings of the complete graph on n labeled vertices. A size-r semidefinite lift is an affine subspace L of the real symmetric \(r\times r\) matrices and an affine map \(\pi\) into \(\mathbb{R}\)^(n choose 2) such that \(\mathrm{P}_{n}=\pi (\mathrm{L}\cap S_{+}^{r})\), where \(S_{+}^{r}\) consists of positive semidefinite matrices. \(xc_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) is the smallest such integer r. Coefficients may be arbitrary real numbers and need not be efficiently generated. The representation is exact; approximate relaxations and linear lifts are different notions.

context_blocks.text: Perfect matching can be optimized in polynomial time, yet exact linear descriptions in higher-dimensional spaces can require exponentially many inequalities. The question asks whether positive semidefinite constraints also suffer a superpolynomial representation barrier.

A linear extension-complexity lower bound is not a semidefinite one. Allowing an arbitrary affine slice of a positive semidefinite cone makes the model substantially stronger. A lower bound here would separate efficient optimization from compact exact SDP representation for a canonical tractable polytope.

why: Identify a fundamental limitation of exact semidefinite optimization representations.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
